title: opentel-mcp: MCP Server Health
description: Failure and cost visibility opentel-mcp adds on top of standard OTel: silent tool failures (isError:true inside a 200 OK), agent thrash loops, tool schema drift, and LLM cost attribution. See dashboards/README.md for setup.

panels.title: Silent failure rate
panels.description: Share of tool calls that returned isError: true inside a successful (200-equivalent) JSON-RPC response — a CallToolResult a standard OTel setup renders as a clean, green, 'successful' span, because no exception was thrown and no error.type was set. This is the failure class opentel-mcp exists to surface. A rising line here means agents are silently getting wrong/failed results and (without this signal) nobody would know from tracing alone.

panels.title: Silent failures by tool
panels.description: mcp.tool.silent_failures broken out by gen_ai.tool.name — which specific tool is producing isError:true responses, and how that's trending. Use this to find the one broken tool instead of just knowing 'something is failing somewhere'.

panels.title: Failure category breakdown
panels.description: mcp.failure.category attached to both mcp.tool.errors (thrown/protocol failures) and mcp.tool.silent_failures (isError:true), summed over the selected time range: auth, timeout, network, dependency, serialization, validation, internal, or unknown. This is opentel-mcp's fingerprinting classifier output, the only fingerprint-derived attribute safe enough (an 8-value closed enum) to put on a metric label — see METRIC_SAFE_ATTRIBUTES in src/fingerprint/attributes.js. Use it to tell 'we have an auth problem' from 'we have a flaky-dependency problem' without opening a single trace.

panels.title: Thrash episodes and wasted cost
panels.description: mcp.tool.loop.detected: the same tool failing with the same failure fingerprint repeatedly (default threshold: 3 consecutive same-fingerprint failures) — an agent stuck retrying a call that will never succeed. Paired with mcp.tool.loop.wasted_cost_usd, the cumulative USD burned by each detected loop so far. A spike in episodes with a corresponding cost spike means agents are burning real money retrying a call that needed a human, not another retry.

panels.title: Schema drift events by tool
panels.description: mcp.tool.schema_drift.detected: a tool's inputSchema changed between two observed tools/list responses, broken out by tool. Schema drift silently breaks agents that cached an older schema or validated arguments against it — this has no standard-OTel equivalent at all (tools/list isn't a tool-call span). A tool showing up here means its contract changed underneath whatever's calling it.

panels.title: Cost by tool
panels.description: mcp.tool.cost.total: estimated USD spend attributed to each tool over the selected range, from mcp.tool.tokens.* and src/cost/calculator.js's pricing table. Only populated for tool calls whose result carries a recognizable token-usage shape (Anthropic/OpenAI/Bedrock conventions) — a tool that never reports usage will never appear here, which is expected, not a bug (see dashboards/README.md).
